To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

electrical stimulation of both the NAcc and CP differentially affects male rat copulatory behavior expression and that the NAcc stimulation effect is not able to reverse the sexual behavior suppression that follows copulation to satiety.
electrical stimulation of both the dorsal and the ventral striatum can facilitate male rat copulatory behavior, but the ventral striatal facilitative effect is stronger.

electrical stimulation of both the nucleus accumbense and the caudate- putamen differentially modulates sexual behavior of male rats, with the stimulation frequency being a relevant variable in this regard.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role that electrical stimulation of striatal brain regions exerts on male sexual behavior expression.
the study of the neural substrates that control sexual activity.
the study of the effects of electrical brain stimulation on the expression of male rat sexual behavior, and its possible relationship to the rewarding properties of sexual behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the striatal DA system exerts an overall facilitative influence on the expression of sexual behavior of sexually experienced male animals.
electrical stimulation of NAcc at the parameters used in the present work is a rewarding stimulus, but that it is insufficient to surmount the sexual exhaustion state.
electrical stimulation of striatum, at the parameters used in the present work, can be rewarding, but it does not necessarily facilitate the expression of copulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
electrical stimulation of NAcc, by increasing the activity of its DAergic neurons, enhances copulatory activity, while CP electrical stimulation inhibits it.
, in male rats, electrical stimulation of the ventral and dorsal striatum differentially modulates sexual behavior expression and the sexual exhaustion state.
electrical stimulation of striatal regions can be used to enhance copulatory activity of male rats, but only when the animals are sexually active and not when sexual exhaustion has taken place.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the striatum is a key brain area in the control of male sexual behavior, but its role is not limited to its dopaminergic innervation.

the NAcc and CP have opposite influences on copulation, which is consistent with the view that the NAcc is a brain region that mediates sexual incentive motivation, whereas the CP mediates sexual consummatory behavior.
the NAcc and CP are differentially involved in male rat sexual behavior, with the former exerting a facilitative influence and the latter an inhibitory influence.
